Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The cost of the worst possible single operation corresponds to the vertex with the maximum number of outgoing edges, which in a simple directed graph is at most |V| - 1. The average amortized cost, computed via aggregate analysis, is the total cost of all |V| operations divided by |V|, which equals |E| / |V| since the sum of all outgoing edges across all vertices equals the total number of edges.

* (a) The worst possible single operation has a cost of **|V| - 1**, which occurs when a vertex has an outgoing edge to every other vertex in the graph.
* (b) The average amortized cost based on aggregate analysis is **|E| / |V|**, because the total cost across all |V| operations equals the total number of edges |E|, and dividing by the number of operations |V| yields the amortized cost per operation.
